r0.why: Transformation of existing rock, metamorphism [1]; protolith, above 150-200 C and often 100 MPa or more [2]; mostly solid, recrystallizes [3]; protolith types [4].

r1.why: Three great divisions [15]; large part of crust and 12% of land surface [5]; deep burial [7]; continental collisions [8]; local heating by magma intrusion [9].

r2.why: Hutton first noted heating [18]; 1795 Scottish Highlands statement [19]; speculated on pressure [20]; Hall's chalk in cannon-barrel vessel [21]; marble-like result rather than quicklime [22].

r3.why: Mineral change without bulk change [29]; stability limits of temperature, pressure, chemical environment [30]; kyanite to andalusite at about 190 C [31]; sillimanite at about 800 C [32]; identical Al2SiO5 [33].

r4.why: Recrystallization defined [38]; calcite crystals grow in marble [39]; sandstone to compact interlocked quartzite [40]; both heat and pressure [41]; migration of atoms and solution at contacts [42].

r5.why: Mineral stability limits indicate approximate temperatures and pressures [44]; index minerals [45]; exposed after erosion and uplift, information on depths of crust [10].

r6.why: Five examples [11]; slate and quartzite tiles [12]; marble for building and sculpture [13]; schist planes of weakness challenge engineering [14].
